images.caption: Arch Point, Santa Barbara Island: With winter rains, the coreopsis emerges from summer's dormancy with light green foliage and bright yellow daisy-like flowers

images.alt: Pine tree high on a ridge overlooking a bay with blue water and white sand beach.
images.caption: Torrey Pines, Santa Rosa Island: Torrey pines occur naturally in only two locations throughout the world--on the cool, fog drenched northeastern slopes of Bechers Bay and just north of San Diego.

images.alt: Brown seals and sea lions on white sand beach with blue water and partly cloudy sky.
images.caption: Point Bennet, San Miguel Island: One of the greatest concentrations of wildlife in the world occurs on San Miguel with over 100,000 pinnipeds gathering to breed, pup, and rest.

images.alt: Rust and grey colored fox in green grass.
images.caption: Island Fox, Santa Cruz Island: Thousands of years of isolation in a unique island environment has resulted in the development of the endemic island fox, a dwarf form of the mainland gray fox.

name: Hiking at Hopewell Furnace National Historic Site
location: Hopewell Furnace National Historic Site, PA
description: Hopewell Furnace showcases an early American landscape of industrial operations from 1771-1883, Hopewell and other iron plantations laid the foundation for the transformation of the United States into an industrial giant
imageAlt: buildings varying in size on either side of a gravel path.

images.alt: buildings varying in size on either side of a gravel path.
images.caption: A community grew around the furnace, it yielded iron and a way of life.

images.alt: Front of Hopewell Furnace's Boarding House
images.caption: Hopewell Furnace's Boarding House housed single men or those living away from their families, who came to work at the furnace.

images.alt: Side view of blacksmith shop with cast house behind it.
images.caption: The Cast House was the industrial center of the ironworks.  It is were iron ore was smelted into iron metal and products.  The smaller blacksmith shop formed iron metal into all kinds of necessary tools and goods used in everyday life.

images.alt: Side view of Hopewell Stove in front of wagon running gear.
images.caption: The most notable manufactured product Hopewell Furnace made was its stoves.  They were produced by the thousands at Hopewell and other like furnaces in the early 19th century and were transported for sale by horse and wagon.

images.alt: Demonstration charcoal pile smoldering.
images.caption: Charcoal was the fuel used to fire Hopewell Furnace and other furnaces of its age.  Thousands of bushles of charcoal were made from hardwood trees on the furnace lands and entered into the furnace to keep it "in blast."
